topics.description: Uploading local commits to a branch on a remote repository, making them visible to collaborators. Committing only records a snapshot in the local repository; nothing reaches the remote until a push. The remote and branch pushed to default to the current branch's configured upstream, so git push -u origin main both pushes and sets that upstream, letting a later bare git push know where to send it. A push that would discard commits already on the remote is refused (a non-fast-forward rejection) unless overridden with --force.
topics.notes: Depth rationale: command-bearing: the exam can ask which command or option fits a stated need.
